name: Duke Energy
tagline: Leading energy company providing reliable and affordable electricity to 8.7 million customers across the Southeast and Midwest
hero_kpi_rationale: Duke Energy dessert 8,7 millions de clients électricité dans 6 États du Sud-Est et du Midwest sur un territoire d'environ 90 000 miles carrés. C'est l'indicateur le plus suivi de l'échelle et du leadership du groupe en tant que fournisseur régulé.

stories_kpis.story_fr: Duke Energy capte une partie importante de la demande charge datacenter dans le Sud-Est, soutenant la croissance pluri-annuelle du parc régulé.
L'objectif de croissance EPS 5-7% par an est désormais relevé en haut de fourchette grâce à la demande datacenter.

risks.title: Government Policy Dependence
risks.score_rationale: Federal or state policies could be enacted that restrict the availability of and increase the costs associated with fuels or generation technologies such as natural gas or nuclear power that enable Duke Energy to reduce its carbon emissions. (Item 1A) (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Government policies can impact Duke Energy's energy strategy and cost structure

risks.title: Regulatory Risks
risks.score_rationale: Duke Energy is subject to regulation by FERC and state utility regulatory agencies which have jurisdiction over rates and investment recovery. Regulatory decisions can materially impact operating results. (Item 1A, Item 4) (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Regulators can limit Duke Energy's ability to recover costs through rate mechanisms

risks.title: Increased Competition
risks.score_rationale: Increased competition in the energy sector may impact Duke Energy's operating results and market share across its service territories. (Item 1A) (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Competition can reduce Duke Energy's market share in key regions

risks.title: Environmental and Climate Risks
risks.score_rationale: Environmental regulations can increase operating costs. Duke Energy must manage coal-fired facility retirements, replacement generation availability, and comply with emission standards. (Item 1A, Item 7) (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Environmental regulations and climate change can impact Duke Energy's energy strategy and asset values

risks.title: Technology Dependence
risks.score_rationale: The availability and deployment of generation and grid technologies can impact Duke Energy's ability to achieve modernization and carbon reduction objectives. (Item 1A) (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Technologies play a key role in Duke Energy's energy modernization strategy

risks.title: Nuclear Operations Risk
risks.score_rationale: Duke Energy operates multiple nuclear facilities including McGuire, Oconee, Catawba, Robinson, Brunswick and Harris. Nuclear liability is capped by the Price-Anderson Act at approximately 16.3 billion dollars. Uninsured losses could materially impact operations. (Item 5) (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Nuclear operations represent significant liability and regulatory exposure

risks.title: Business Strategy Implementation
risks.score_rationale: Duke Energy's future results depend on successfully implementing its business strategy to provide reliable energy while maintaining low costs and balancing modernization with carbon reduction objectives amid regulatory uncertainties. (Item 1A) (score par défaut, à affiner)
risks.summary: Execution on strategic objectives is subject to business, policy, regulatory and economic uncertainties

company_description: Duke Energy Corporation, through its subsidiaries, operates as an energy company in the United States. The company operates through two segments: Electric Utilities and Infrastructure (EU&I); and Gas Utilities and Infrastructure (GU&I). The EU&I segment generates, transmits, distributes, and sells electricity to customers in the Southeast and Midwest regions. It generates electricity through coal, hydroelectric, natural gas, oil, renewables, and nuclear fuel. This segment also engages in the wholesale of electricity to municipalities, electric cooperative utilities, and other load-serving entities. The GU&I segment distributes natural gas to customers in the residential, commercial, industrial, and power generation natural gas sectors; and invests in pipeline transmission projects, renewable natural gas projects, and natural gas storage facilities. The company was formerly known as Duke Energy Holding Corp. and changed its name to Duke Energy Corporation in April 2006. Duke Energy Corporation was founded in 1904 and is headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina.
